metadata.title: Runs the Steps. Doesn't Write the CIM.
metadata.subtitle: The CIM-Builder Skill (Financial Services)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to build a CIM, is it writing the deal story from scratch, or running a fixed spec on what you give it? Lands the carry-out that cim-builder doesn't author judgment — it runs the SKILL.md's steps on your inputs, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Assume cim-builder writes your CIM and you'll be disappointed. Here's what's actually happening — a fixed set of steps that structure one, run the same way each time. So: does cim-builder structure my CIM?

TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 1.0 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('write' -> 'structure') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder — that's the whole mechanism. This one, cim-builder, holds one file: SKILL.md, plain English, no hidden logic underneath. Claude opens it, reads it top to bottom, acts on it. The file is the program. They optimized for readability over cleverness.
The instructions live in a Steps section. Claude reads them in order and executes — one after another, straight through. No branching, unless a step itself asks for it. Linearity is the whole point.

production_viz.label: ONE STEP AT A TIME
production_viz.caption: no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: cim-builder's job is deliberately narrow. Structure and draft a Confidential Information Memorandum for a sell-side deal — take the company information you feed it, organize it into one investor-ready document, consistent formatting, a narrative that holds together, the same shape every run. Anything the SKILL.md's steps don't cover isn't part of the job. The tradeoff is consistency for range: same output shape every time, at the cost of anything novel.
cim-builder doesn't write your CIM. It runs the SKILL.md's fixed steps on it — the same steps, the same way, every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to structure and draft a Confidential Information Memorandum for a sell-side M&A process. Read the cim-builder skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That last clause is the whole trick — asking Claude to narrate its plan before running surfaces the actual steps, not a polished summary of them. Go deeper: after Claude runs the skill on your data, ask it which sections it had to invent from thin material — that's where your own judgment has to land.
